sentences.text: Orodromeus was a small, plant-eating dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America. Its name, meaning "Mountain Runner," highlights its likely running abilities and the Egg Mountain site where it was found.
Scientists estimated this animal to be about 2.5 meters long and noted it possessed a strong jugal bone, a skull feature also seen in the relative Zephyrosaurus.
Ten nests containing eggs arranged in a spiral pattern have been discovered, and CT scans revealed the unhatched embryos were remarkably well-developed.
Unlike the helpless hatchlings of Maiasaura, Orodromeus young likely abandoned their nests immediately after hatching, as the empty shells show no signs of being trampled.
Researchers speculate that Orodromeus may have burrowed, a behavior suggested by the unusual packing of its fossil bones, similar to its relative Oryctodromeus.

The fossils were found by Robert Makela while he was digging up a nesting colony of Maiasaura in Teton County, Montana. The species name makelai honors him, even though he died in a car accident shortly after the discovery.

Jack Horner and David B. Weishampel named the species Orodromeus makelai in 1988. The holotype specimen, the specific specimen the species is based on, came from the Campanian stage of the Two Medicine Formation.
In 1990, Laosaurus minimus was considered a second species of Orodromeus, though this assignment remains uncertain due to fragmentary remains.
Jack Horner concluded that Orodromeus young were precocial, meaning they were relatively mature and mobile from the moment of hatching, based on the advanced development of their bones and teeth.

The dinosaur nested in large colonies where individual nests were excavated and covered to better control temperature. It appears that Orodromeus parents cared for their nests by driving away small predators.

Modern classification views Orodromeus as a basal member of the Euornithopoda, as the group Hypsilophodontidae is considered unnatural and paraphyletic. Brown et al. (2013) classified Orodromeus in the family Thescelosauridae and named the subfamily Orodrominae after it.
Orodromeus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago. This small herbivore likely coexisted with dinosaurs such as Daspletosaurus and Einiosaurus.
Several Orodromeus nests were found alongside those of Maiasaura.
